cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.summary: At the foot of the page, the haloed Christ sits in a large medallion holding a book, flanked by smaller roundels containing the winged symbols of the evangelists. The lower margin of the leaf is damaged.
facts: Its pictures interpret the psalms literally, historically or — very often — Christologically, as prophecies of the life of Christ.
The manuscript came to Württemberg under Duke Charles Eugene (its sale is first mentioned in 1787) and has been in the library at Stuttgart since at least 1818.
cur:manuscripts-stuttgart-psalter-psalm-.notes: Image from the WLB digital facsimile (Public Domain Mark), showing the whole page with the miniature. The exact verse is not legible at this resolution.

cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-2-christ-.summary: On a hill in the centre of the sketchy landscape stands the nimbed Christ-Logos, given power by a great Hand of God reaching down from the heavens, while the raging 'people' and the kings who conspire against the Lord crowd the valleys below. He holds the 'rod of iron' with which the psalm says he will break the nations like a potter's vessel. It is one of the clearest early images of the psalm's messianic king read as Christ.
facts: The Utrecht Psalter illustrates every psalm and canticle with a lively pen drawing — 166 in all — that translates the words of the text, often literally, into images; in these the Lord of the psalms is regularly shown as the youthful Christ-Logos.
The psalter was made in or near Reims, probably under Archbishop Ebbo (816–835); some scholars argue for a date around 850 under his successor Hincmar.
cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-2-christ-.notes: The figure of the Lord is identified as Christ (the Christ-Logos) following the commentary of the Utrecht University Library's annotated edition, which describes the psalter's consistent practice of drawing the God of the psalms as the youthful Christ. The image is a crop of the drawing from the library's IIIF image server.

cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-79-christ.summary: Christ appears twice: above, the Christ-Logos holding a book sits in a mandorla supported by cherubim and flanked by angels, the Shepherd of Israel 'that dwellest between the cherubims'; below him stands Christ, beardless and cross-nimbed, as 'the son of man whom thou madest strong for thyself', with a wreath above his head. Figures identified as Joseph, Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh stand on either side, with sheep nearby.
